item.text:
## 2B.1 Research Note: Kishida in 2024

Overall reading: **yes, often.** In 2024 Kishida repeatedly chose diplomacy, multilateral process, and channel-preserving de-escalation when peaceful routes existed, especially on North Korea, Ukraine, and nuclear risk. The main counterevidence is that he paired this with a stronger deterrence and alliance posture, so the year is **not** pure de-escalation.

### Supports
- **Japan-Ukraine Summit Telephone Talk (Summary)** | Prime Minister's Office of Japan | April 3, 2024 | https://japan.kantei.go.jp/101_kishida/diplomatic/202404/03ukraine.html  
  Kishida told Zelenskyy Japan would “never waver” in standing with Ukraine and said both sides would continue to work closely together. This is evidence of choosing diplomatic coordination and support for a peaceful settlement track over force-first escalation.  
  Question IDs: `2B.1`, `1B.8`, `1B.4`

- **Why is Japan seeking a summit with nuclear-armed North Korea?** | Reuters | April 11, 2024 | https://www.investing.com/news/world-news/explainerwhy-is-japan-seeking-a-summit-with-nucleararmed-north-korea-3374282  
  Reuters reported Kishida wanted face-to-face talks with Kim Jong Un, and Biden publicly called dialogue a good thing. This is direct evidence that Kishida preferred diplomacy with a nuclear-armed adversary rather than treating force as the first option.  
  Question IDs: `2B.1`, `1B.8`, `1B.4`, `1B.6`

- **The Ninth Japan-China-ROK Trilateral Summit (Summary)** | Prime Minister’s Office of Japan | May 27, 2024 | https://japan.kantei.go.jp/101_kishida/diplomatic/202405/27chnrok.html  
  Kishida used a multilateral forum to urge North Korea to completely abandon its nuclear and ballistic missile programs in line with UN Security Council resolutions. That is a de-escalatory, diplomatic route aimed at peaceful alternatives rather than coercion.  
  Question IDs: `2B.1`, `1B.4`, `1B.6`, `1B.8`

- **Address by Prime Minister KISHIDA Fumio at the Hiroshima Peace Memorial Ceremony** | Prime Minister’s Office of Japan | August 6, 2024 | https://japan.kantei.go.jp/101_kishida/statement/202408/06hiroshima.html  
  Kishida reaffirmed the Three Non-Nuclear Principles, rejected repeating Hiroshima and Nagasaki, and argued for realistic progress through the NPT and FMCT routes. This is strong evidence of de-escalation and diplomacy where peaceful alternatives clearly existed.  
  Question IDs: `2B.1`, `1B.1`, `1B.2`, `1B.4`, `1B.8`

- **Summit on Peace in Ukraine (Summary)** | Prime Minister’s Office of Japan | June 15, 2024 | https://japan.kantei.go.jp/101_kishida/diplomatic/202406/15ukraine.html  
  Kishida emphasized a “just and lasting peace” based on the UN Charter and said peace should not justify unilateral changes by force or coercion. He also said Japan would contribute on nuclear safety and mine action. This is clear peace-process framing, not force-first thinking.  
  Question IDs: `2B.1`, `1B.8`, `1B.9`, `1B.4`

### Cuts against / limits
- **Address by Prime Minister at a Joint Meeting of the United States Congress** | Prime Minister’s Office of Japan | April 11, 2024 | https://japan.kantei.go.jp/101_kishida/statement/202404/11speech.html  
  Kishida highlighted counterstrike capability, defense spending, cyber capability, and stronger U.S. extended deterrence. This is not a force-first doctrine by itself, but it shows he did not choose diplomacy alone when peaceful alternatives existed.  
  Question IDs: `2B.1`, `1B.4`, `1B.8`, `1B.9`

- **Press Conference by Prime Minister Kishida regarding His Attendance at the NATO Summit and Other Matters** | Prime Minister’s Office of Japan | July 11, 2024 | https://japan.kantei.go.jp/101_kishida/statement/202407/11kaiken.html  
  Kishida said Euro-Atlantic and Indo-Pacific security are inseparable and expanded Japan-NATO cooperation on cyber, space, information-sharing, and support for Ukraine. This is structured alliance de-escalation in some dimensions, but it also embeds Japan more deeply in deterrence and bloc competition.  
  Question IDs: `2B.1`, `1B.4`, `1B.8`, `1B.9`

### Search gap
- I found **strong evidence for diplomacy and compromise** on North Korea, Ukraine, and nuclear disarmament.
- I found **no 2024 evidence** that Kishida treated force as his preferred first option in a live crisis.
- The best calibration is **mostly yes on diplomacy/de-escalation, mixed because he simultaneously expanded deterrence and alliance hardening.**
